objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing transducer array element failure rate per 1000 hours of operation
independent_variables: Nucleus embedded between transducer array elements and imaging electronics
dependent_variables: Transducer array element failure rate per 1000 hours of operation
controls: Current transducer array element failure rate per 1000 hours of operation (average of 5 previous prototypes)
baseline: Current transducer array element failure rate per 1000 hours of operation (average of 5 previous prototypes)
procedure: Prepare 10 identical transducer array elements with the Nucleus embedded between the transducer array elements and the imaging electronics
Prepare 10 identical transducer array elements without the Nucleus
Subject both sets of transducer array elements to 1000 hours of continuous operation at 50°C
Monitor and record the failure rate of each transducer array element
expected_result: A 30% decrease in transducer array element failure rate per 1000 hours of operation
falsification_condition: Failure rate per 1000 hours of operation increases by more than 10% compared to the baseline, or the thermal-mechanical coupling mechanism is found to be ineffective in experimental data or simulations
sample_requirements: 10 identical transducer array elements with the Nucleus and 10 identical transducer array elements without the Nucleus
safety_constraints: Ensure that the transducer array elements are operated within their specified temperature and power limits to prevent damage or injury
information_gain: Validation of the Nucleus' effectiveness in reducing transducer array element failure rate and understanding of the thermal-mechanical coupling mechanism's impact on transducer array element reliability
